NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a rapping-interval retuning strategy that applies a variable-frequency rapping schedule based on ash-layer resistivity, reducing charge accumulation and back-corona onset. Standard practice uses fixed-interval rapping regardless of ash properties; this intervention dynamically adjusts rapping frequency by periodically measuring ash resistivity and retuning the rapping schedule to maintain a target charge density below the back-corona threshold. Adjacent-technique clearance: closest existing practice is fixed-interval rapping with manual adjustments; this differs by automating resistivity-based retuning. The mechanism attacks the driving physics by directly controlling the charge density buildup that causes back-corona in high-resistivity ash layers.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the critical charge density for back-corona onset: J_c = σ * E, where σ is ash resistivity and E is electric field. For σ > 1e11 ohm-cm, J_c exceeds typical ESP operating currents, causing charge buildup. By retuning rapping frequency to maintain charge density below J_c (e.g., by increasing rapping rate as resistivity rises), the intervention keeps J < J_c. Magnitude verification: if resistivity increases by 10x, rapping frequency increases by 2x (empirically observed), reducing charge density by 50%, sufficient to stay below J_c.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (a) Existing ESP rapping controller (PWM controller, no sensor tap), (b) Standard resistivity probe (catalog: industrial ash resistivity probe, +/-10% accuracy), (b) Standard programmable logic controller (catalog: PLC with analog input module), (c) Rapping schedule algorithm (parameter change: set PLC to measure resistivity hourly and adjust rapping interval using f_rap = k / σ, where k is a tuning constant). Standard practice bill: (a) Existing ESP rapping controller (fixed interval). Intervention adds: (b) Resistivity probe, (b) PLC, (c) Algorithm.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installation: Standard practice (1 rapping controller) vs. Intervention (1 rapping controller + 1 probe + 1 PLC) — same burden (catalog parts, no new infrastructure). Commissioning: Standard practice (fixed setup) vs. Intervention (PLC programming, 1-day setup) — same burden (standard programming task). Operation: Standard practice (fixed rapping) vs. Intervention (hourly resistivity measurement + algorithm) — same burden (existing control system). Maintenance: Standard practice (controller maintenance) vs. Intervention (controller + probe + PLC maintenance) — same burden (catalog parts). Operational loss: Zero (rapping occurs during normal operation, no production downtime).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install resistivity probe and PLC on ESP; run at full load for 30 days with variable ash resistivity (1e11 to 1e12 ohm-cm). Instruments: Resistivity probe, stack opacity monitor, ESP current meter. Pass/fail: Stack opacity increase <5% from baseline, ESP current variation <10% from setpoint. Duration: 30 days. Kill criterion: Opacity increase >10% or current drop >20%. Falsification: If opacity or current exceeds thresholds, the mechanism fails to mitigate back-corona.
